newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares end lower in record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares end lower in record turnover.

text.p: Profit-taking knocked down key banking stocks on the Tallinn bourse on Wednesday as it surged to record turnover, dealers said.
Turnover was a record 184.46 million kroons compared to the previous peak of 178.8 million kroons set a week ago.
The stock exchange has been exceptionally active for the last two weeks as the market waits for upward profit forecast revisions after better than expected interim results.
Foreign investors have also buoyed trade in the wake of the European Commission's announcement last week that Estonia had made the grade for the first round of EU entry talks.
But dealers said that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks that U.S. economic growth had moderated had little to do with the record turnover.
Dealers said continuous profit-taking in Hansapank, Hoiupank and Forekspank, which climbed to new highs last week, pulled the index down by 1.10 percent to 338.49.
One dealer said their prices should remain stable for the rest of the week ahead of the expected upward revision in their profit forecasts.
Uhispank was higher again by 4.05 kroons to close at 68.30 kroons.
Dealers said it looks like a bargain at its current price.
On the free market, Norma was the most active stock in trade of 14.57 million kroons to lose 0.38 kroons to 87.62 kroons.

The stock has been active since its parent company sold some 11.9 percent of its shares to western investors. The market is also waiting for its revised profit forecast after strong half-year results, dealers said.
